paragraphs: Arbutus Biopharma Corporation ("Arbutus", the "Company", "we", "us", and "our") is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on infectious disease. We are currently developing imdusiran (AB-729), our proprietary, GalNAc-conjugated, subcutaneously-delivered ribonucleic acid interference (RNAi) therapeutic, and AB-101, our proprietary oral PD-L1 inhibitor, for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (cHBV).

We continue to protect and defend our intellectual property, which is the subject of our ongoing lawsuit against Pfizer Inc. and BioNTech SE (collectively, Pfizer/BioNTech) for their use of our patented lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology in their COVID-19 messenger ribonucleic acid interference (mRNA)-LNP vaccines. The court issued a claim construction ruling in September 2025, which construed the disputed claim terms in a manner we generally consider to be favorable. The parties are awaiting further scheduling in the litigation.

On March 3, 2026, we, along with Genevant Sciences GmbH and its parent (collectively, Genevant), entered into a settlement agreement (the Moderna Settlement Agreement) to resolve all patent infringement litigation and patent revocation proceedings involving Moderna, Inc. and its affiliates (collectively, Moderna) pending in the United States and internationally (the Moderna LNP Litigation). Under the terms of the Moderna Settlement Agreement, Moderna will make an aggregate $950.0 million noncontingent lump sum payment (the Noncontingent Settlement Payment) to us and Genevant on or before July 8, 2026. In addition, Moderna is obligated to pay us and Genevant an additional aggregate contingent lump sum payment of $1.3 billion (the Contingent Settlement Payment) upon a ruling that is favorable to us and Genevant in a limited appeal related to 28 U.S.C. §1498 (§1498) that Moderna is allowed to file pursuant to the Moderna Settlement Agreement (the Moderna §1498 Appeal). Under our license with Genevant, we are entitled to receive, after deduction of litigation costs, 20% of the Noncontingent Settlement Payment. In addition, as of the date of this annual report, we own approximately 16% of the outstanding common equity of Genevant. We are currently evaluating a return of capital to our shareholders in the third quarter of calendar year 2026, following the receipt of our portion of the Noncontingent Settlement Payment. For more information, see "Item 1 – Business – Other Collaborations, Royalty Entitlements and Intellectual Property Litigation" and "Item 3 – Legal Proceedings."

During 2024, we streamlined the organization to focus our efforts on advancing the clinical development of imdusiran and AB-101, and therefore ceased all discovery efforts, halted preparations for a potential IM-PROVE III clinical trial and reduced our workforce by 40%. In the first quarter of 2025, we announced the appointment of five new members of our Board of Directors (our Board) to replace all of the former directors, as well as the appointment of a new President, Chief Executive Officer and Chairperson of our Board and a new Chief Financial Officer. Additionally, our Board took action to reduce our workforce by an additional 57%. Our Board also decided to exit our corporate headquarters in Warminster, Pennsylvania and to discontinue in-house scientific research. In connection with these actions, we incurred one-time restructuring charges during 2025 of $12.9 million. With these organizational changes and our ongoing cost management efforts, we significantly reduced our net cash burn in 2025 when compared to 2024.

In June 2025, we launched a new Scientific Advisory Board (SAB) consisting of globally-recognized leaders in the treatment of cHBV with extensive experience in late-stage clinical trials. SAB members are advising us on the strategic evaluation of our cHBV pipeline.

In August 2025, we announced changes to our Board. Effective August 4, 2025, Anuj Hasija resigned from our Board due to his transition to a full-time executive role at another company that precludes his participation on our Board and other boards of directors. Dr. Roger Sawhney was appointed to the vacant seat on our Board, effective August 4, 2025. Dr. Sawhney was also appointed as a member of our Board's Audit Committee and Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee.
Our strategy is focused on maximizing opportunities for our cHBV development programs and, through our exclusive license with Genevant, our in-house developed LNP technology.

In February 2022 and April 2023, we filed patent infringement lawsuits in the United States against Moderna and Pfizer/BioNTech, respectively, seeking compensation for their unlicensed use of our patented technologies in their COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines. It is well established in the scientific literature that the most significant technological hurdle to developing and deploying medicines using mRNA is engineering a safe and effective way to deliver the mRNA to human cells. Scientists at Arbutus and Genevant have spent years developing and refining LNP technology, which has been licensed for various applications to many different third parties. Our and Genevant's LNP technology relies on microscopic particles built from four carefully selected types of fat-like molecules to shelter and protect nucleic acid molecules, including ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules like the messenger RNA (mRNA) utilized in COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines. This technology enables the mRNA to travel through the human body to a target cell and through the target cell's membrane, where it releases the mRNA. Without this crucial technology, the mRNA would quickly degrade in the body and be ineffective. We continue to protect and defend our intellectual property, which is the subject of our ongoing lawsuit against Pfizer/BioNTech for their use of our patented LNP technology in their COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines.

Our hepatitis B (HBV) strategy has been to develop a functional cure for patients with cHBV infection with imdusiran as a potential cornerstone in a combination therapy. Development to date has emphasized a combination of compounds that can suppress hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid (HBV DNA) replication, hepatitis B virus RNA (HBV RNA) transcription, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and other viral protein expression, as well as boost patients' HBV-specific immune response, which together could address the most important elements to achieving a functional cure. Functional cure is defined as sustained HBsAg seroclearance and HBV DNA less than the lower limit of quantification (<LLOQ) after 24 weeks off treatment, with or without anti-hepatitis B surface antibodies (anti-HBs). A functional cure for patients with cHBV could prevent complications of HBV disease progression, decrease HBV burden by minimizing patient stigma and address the need for finite and more efficacious HBV treatments that further improve long-term outcomes and reduce associated healthcare costs. Our current ongoing evaluation of our HBV strategy also includes analysis of imdusiran's potential to suppress HBV DNA replication and HBV RNA and HBsAg expression, without any immunotherapeutics. We are also continuing to evaluate and refine potential Phase 2b clinical trial designs for imdusiran.
Our HBV product pipeline includes the following:

•Imdusiran (AB-729) is our proprietary, GalNAc-conjugated, subcutaneously-delivered RNAi therapeutic product candidate that suppresses all HBV antigens, including HBsAg, which is thought to be a key prerequisite to enable potentiation of a patient's immune system to respond to HBV. Over 200 patients with cHBV infection have been dosed with imdusiran in Phase 1 and Phase 2a clinical trials. Clinical data generated thus far has shown imdusiran provides meaningful reductions in HBsAg and other viral proteins, HBV DNA and HBV RNA, and leads to functional cure in some patients, while being generally safe and well-tolerated. Benefits were observed in patients across all evaluated HBV genotypes (A to E). In the Phase 1 and Phase 2a clinical trials, eight patients achieved functional cure, off all treatment, in combination therapy that includes imdusiran, including two patients who did not receive any pegylated interferon alfa-2a (IFN) as part of the combination therapy. An additional 41 patients across our Phase 2a clinical trials were able to remain off nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for at least 48 weeks after discontinuing NA therapy during their Phase 2a clinical trials. A total of 47% (49/105) of all Phase 2a patients achieved functional cure or remained off NA therapy after discontinuing NA therapy during their Phase 2a clinical trials. Of the 18 patients who are currently being followed long-term (which includes the eight functionally cured patients described above and 10 patients who discontinued and remained off NA therapy), one patient who discontinued NA therapy achieved functional cure during the long-term follow-up period, and 89% of the 18 patients continue to remain off NA therapy for between 82 and 134 weeks. Two of the original eight functionally cured patients seroreverted during long-term follow-up, but remain virally suppressed and off NA therapy. Furthermore, among an additional 11 patients with available data who discontinued NA therapy during their Phase 2a clinical trials, but were subsequently discontinued early from long-term follow-up, one patient achieved functional cure and two restarted NA therapy. To date, a total of 10 patients have achieved functional cure during our Phase 2a clinical trials and long-term follow-up.

•AB-101 is our proprietary oral PD-L1 inhibitor that has the potential to activate patients' HBV-specific immune response by inhibiting PD-L1. AB-101 is currently in a Phase 1a/1b clinical trial (AB-101-001) evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of single- and multiple-ascending oral doses in healthy subjects and patients with cHBV infection. The data from healthy subjects in Parts 1 and 2 and cHBV patients in Part 3 of this clinical trial have shown that AB-101 was generally well-tolerated with evidence of high receptor occupancy.

To help position imdusiran as a potential cornerstone in a combination therapy, we fully enrolled two Phase 2a clinical trials that combined imdusiran with other agents. The intent of these trials was to initially lower HBsAg levels with imdusiran and then administer a complementary agent, an immune modulator or a therapeutic vaccine, to further lower HBsAg levels and promote anti-HBV immunity. We believe that if we can lower HBsAg and other viral antigens and promote immunity, we may achieve sustained HBsAg seroclearance and HBV DNA <LLOQ, potentially leading to a functional cure in patients with cHBV. Currently, patients with cHBV have limited treatment options - either NA therapy, which requires lifelong treatment, or a finite duration of IFN, which is poorly tolerated and has serious complications and side effects. We believe patients can see significant benefits with imdusiran even without functional cure if they are well enough to be able to discontinue NA therapy and maintain viral suppression.

In the Phase 2a clinical trials, eight patients with cHBV achieved functional cure following treatment with imdusiran and NA therapy in combination with either IFN or with low dose nivolumab plus an immunotherapeutic. Seven of those eight total patients who achieved functional cure with the 60mg dose of imdusiran had HBsAg levels less than 1000 IU/mL at baseline. According to the literature, patients with HBsAg levels <1000 IU/mL represent a significant portion of the cHBV population. To date, six of those eight patients continue to sustain functional cure for periods ranging between 82 to 134 weeks, while two patients have seroreverted but remain virally suppressed and off NA therapy. In addition to the patients who achieved functional cure during their Phase 2a clinical trials, 41 more patients were able to remain off NA therapy for at least 48 weeks during their clinical trials after discontinuing NA therapy following treatment with imdusiran. In total, 47% (49/105) of all Phase 2a patients either achieved functional cure or remained off NA therapy after discontinuing NA therapy during their clinical trials following treatment with imdusiran. Of the 10 patients who were able to discontinue and remain off NA therapy for at least 48 weeks who are currently being followed long-term in our rollover study, one patient achieved functional cure during the long-term follow-up period, and a total of eight patients have continued to remain off NA therapy for periods ranging between 96 to 131 weeks. These results suggest that imdusiran has lasting durability in helping patients maintain viral suppression and may help patients achieve beneficial clinical outcomes years after completing finite imdusiran regimens.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Our Financial Results and Need for Additional Capital
We face risks associated with the Contingent Settlement Payment under the Moderna Settlement Agreement.
We are in the early stages of our development, and there is a limited amount of information about us upon which you can evaluate our product candidates.

We have incurred operating losses in nearly every year since our inception and we anticipate that we will not achieve operating profits for the foreseeable future. To date, we have had no product revenues.
We do not generate revenues from product sales and may never be profitable from operations.
Risks Related to Development, Clinical Testing, Regulatory Approval, Marketing, and Coverage and Reimbursement of our Product Candidates

Because we have limited operational resources, we may decide to pursue a particular product candidate and fail to advance product candidates that later demonstrate a greater chance of clinical and commercial success.
Several of our clinical trials are currently or were conducted outside the United States, and the FDA may not accept data from trials conducted in locations outside the United States.

We cannot guarantee how long it will take regulatory agencies to review our applications for product candidates, and we may fail to obtain the necessary regulatory approvals to market our product candidates.
If a particular product candidate causes undesirable side effects, then we may be unable to receive regulatory approval of or commercialize such product candidate.
We may find it difficult to enroll patients in our clinical trials, which could delay or prevent clinical trials of our product candidates.
Even if our product candidates obtain regulatory approval, they will remain subject to ongoing regulatory requirements and oversight.
We face significant competition from other biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies targeting HBV.
Our ability to generate product revenues and become profitable from operations is largely dependent on the future commercial success of our HBV product candidates.
We may incur substantial liabilities and may be required to limit commercialization of our products in response to product liability lawsuits.
Coverage and adequate reimbursement may not be available for our product candidates, which could make it difficult for us to sell our products profitably.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to substantial risks and uncertainties. The occurrence of any of the following risks and uncertainties, either alone or taken together, could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects. In these circumstances, the market price of our common shares could decline and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Risks and uncertainties of general applicability and additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects.

We are involved in patent infringement lawsuits to protect and assert our intellectual property rights against large, well-capitalized companies and the United States, which requires that we continue to expend substantial resources, and we may not be successful in these proceedings.

We are currently involved in a patent infringement lawsuit in the United States against Pfizer/BioNTech and, if filed by Moderna, the Moderna §1498 Appeal, which are actions against large, well-capitalized companies. We are also involved in a lawsuit against the United States in the United States Court of Federal Claims, seeking to recover compensation for Moderna's infringement for vaccine doses that were sold to the United States Government under a particular contract and were deemed by the District Court to be doses that were provided directly to United States Government employees. Some of these lawsuits have been ongoing for years and have required substantial investments of resources. We anticipate that these proceedings will continue to require similar investments over an extended period of time. Each of the proceedings is subject to substantial uncertainty regarding their outcomes, which is highly dependent upon specific factual matters and legal interpretations. We believe that it is critical to our future success to continue to pursue these actions, and we intend to do so. Each action will result in court rulings and decisions about significant issues, such as claim construction, patent validity, infringement, the affirmative defense under §1498, jurisdiction and other matters, almost all of which are subject to appeal processes that are typically lengthy and unpredictable in terms of outcome. Moreover, the ruling or decision in one proceeding is not necessarily indicative of rulings or decisions that may be issued in another proceeding, even if the factual and legal matters are similar. We expect that various courts will issue significant rulings within the next year, and the disclosure of those rulings may cause substantial volatility in our share price and could impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

In addition to the aggregate $950.0 million Noncontingent Settlement Payment due to us and Genevant, the Moderna Settlement Agreement provides for a Contingent Settlement Payment of up to an aggregate $1.3 billion to us and Genevant, which is payable in full only upon the occurrence of an Arbutus/Genevant §1498 Victory (as defined above). If the appellate court determines that §1498 bars all or some of our and Genevant's claims, we may receive no payment at all or only a prorated portion of the $1.3 billion Contingent Settlement Payment. While Moderna is subject to financial covenants under the Moderna Settlement Agreement to protect the payment of the Contingent Settlement Payment, there can be no assurance that we and Genevant will receive this payment in a timely manner, or at all, due to factors beyond our control, including, among others, the satisfaction of contractual conditions, administrative or procedural delays, or disputes regarding the interpretation or enforcement of the Moderna Settlement Agreement. Moreover, under certain circumstances specified in the Moderna Settlement Agreement, if an Arbutus/Genevant §1498 Victory is subsequently overturned in Moderna's favor in a final, non‑appealable decision, we and Genevant would be required to return any Contingent Settlement Payment previously received, together with interest. Any obligation to repay such amounts could require us to use a significant portion of our available cash. Additionally, any Contingent Settlement Payment we do receive may be subject to financial covenants on us to protect the potential repayment of the Contingent Settlement Payment, which would restrict our ability to freely use those proceeds during that period. The Moderna §1498 Appeal and any subsequent related appeals are subject to substantial uncertainty regarding their outcomes, including the timing thereof, and there can be no assurance that an Arbutus/Genevant §1498 Victory will be achieved. For more information, see "Item 1 – Business – Other Collaborations, Royalty Entitlements and Intellectual Property Litigation" and "Item 3 – Legal Proceedings."

Our expectation of receiving proceeds from the Moderna Settlement Agreement, including through the Genevant License and our equity ownership interest in Genevant, may not be realized. Any delay in receiving such payments, failure to receive some or all of the proceeds under the Moderna Settlement Agreement, or an obligation to return any Contingent Settlement Payments
previously received could materially adversely affect our liquidity, financial condition, results of operations, and ability to execute our business strategy.

paragraphs: Arbutus Biopharma Corporation ("Arbutus", the "Company", "we", "us", and "our") 為一間臨牀階段的生技藥品公司，專注於傳染病領域。我們目前正開發 imdusiran (AB-729)，為我們專屬的 GalNAc 連結零組件，皮下給藥的 RNA 幹擾 (RNAi) 治療藥物，以及 AB-101，為我們專屬的口服 PD-L1 抑製劑，用於治療慢性乙型肝炎 (cHBV)。

我們持續保護並捍衛我們的智慧財產權，這也是我們對 Pfizer Inc. 和 BioNTech SE (合稱 Pfizer/BioNTech) 提起的訴訟內容，他們使用我們專利的脂質奈米粒子 (LNP) 技術在其 COVID-19 消息核糖核酸幹擾 (mRNA)-LNP 疫苗中。法院於 2025 年 9 月發佈了請求項解釋判決，解釋爭議的請求項內容，我們認為這解釋對我們而言通常是有利的。雙方正在等待進一步的訴訟排期。

於 2026 年 3 月 3 日，我們與 Genevant Sciences GmbH 及其母公司 (合稱 Genevant) 籤訂和解協議 (ModernA 和解協議)，以解決所有涉及 Moderna, Inc. 及其子公司 (合稱 Moderna) 在美國及國際上進行的專利侵權訴訟及專利廢止程序 (ModernA LNP 訴訟)。根據 ModernA 和解協議的條款，ModernA 將於 2026 年 7 月 8 日前支付我們及 Genevant 總計 950.0 百萬美元 (Noncontingent Settlement Payment) 的非條件性一次過付款。此外，ModernA 有義務支付我們及 Genevant 總計 1.3 十億美元 (Contingent Settlement Payment) 的條件性一次過付款，前提是於 ModernA 可根據 ModernA 和解協議提出的有限上訴 (ModernA §1498 Appeal) 中，判決對我們及 Genevant 有利。根據我們與 Genevant 的授權協議，我們在扣除訴訟費用後，可獲得 Noncontingent Settlement Payment 的 20%。此外，截至本年度報告日，我們持有 Genevant 約 16% 的流通普通股。我們目前正在評估於 2026 年財年第三季向股東回饋資本，這是在收到我們應得的 Noncontingent Settlement Payment 之後。如需更多資訊，請參閱 "項目 1 – 事業 – 其他合作夥伴、版稅權利及智慧財產權訴訟" 以及 "項目 3 – 法律程序"。

在 2024 年，我們重整組織，專注於推進 imdusiran 和 AB-101 的臨牀開發，因此停止了所有調查工作，中止了潛在的 IM-PROVE III 臨牀試驗準備，並裁減了 40% 的員工。在 2025 年第一季，我們宣佈任命五位新的董事會成員 (董事會) 以取代所有前任董事，以及任命新的總裁、首席執行官、董事會主席及首席財務官。此外，董事會也採取行動，進一步裁減了 57% 的員工。董事會也決定退出位於賓夕法尼亞州 Warminster 的公司總部，並停止內部科學研究。與這些行動相關，我們在 2025 年產生了一次性重組費用 12.9 百萬美元。透過這些組織變更及持續的成本管理措施，我們在 2025 年的淨現金消耗大幅減少，與 2024 年相比。
於 2025 年 6 月，我們啟動了一個新的科學顧問委員會 (SAB)，由 globally-recognized 在 cHBV 治療領域的領導者組成，並擁有豐富的晚期臨牀試驗經驗。SAB 成員正在為我們評估 cHBV 管線的戰略方向提供建議。
於 2025 年 8 月，我們宣佈董事會的變動。自 2025 年 8 月 4 日起，Anuj Hasija 因轉任另一家公司的全職執行長職務，而辭去董事會成員職務，此職務使其無法參與我們董事會及其他董事會。Dr. Roger Sawhney 被任命為董事會的空缺席位，自 2025 年 8 月 4 日起生效。Dr. Sawhney 也同時被任命為我們董事會的審計委員會及企業治理與提名委員會成員。
我們的策略聚焦於最大化我們 cHBV 開發計畫的機會，並透過我們與 Genevant 的獨家授權，我們自有的 LNP 技術。

於 2022 年 2 月及 2023 年 4 月，我們在美國對 Moderna 和 Pfizer/BioNTech 提起專利侵權訴訟，要求賠償他們未經授權使用我們專利技術在他們的 COVID-19 mRNA-LNP 疫苗中。科學文獻已明確指出，開發和部署使用 mRNA 的藥物時，最重要的技術難題是工程一個安全有效的 mRNA 交付方式。Arbutus 和 Genevant 的科學家們已經投入多年時間開發和改進 LNP 技術，該技術已授權給許多不同的第三方用於各種應用。我們與 Genevant 的 LNP 技術依賴於由四種精心選擇的脂肪類分子組成的微小粒子，用以保護和包覆核酸分子，包括核糖核酸 (RNA) 分子，如用於 COVID-19 mRNA-LNP 疫苗中的訊息核糖核酸 (mRNA)。此技術使 mRNA 能夠通過人體到達目標細胞，並透過目標細胞的膜，釋放 mRNA。若沒有這項關鍵技術，mRNA 將會在體內迅速分解且無效。我們持續保護並捍衛我們的智慧財產權，這也是我們對 Pfizer/BioNTech 提起的訴訟內容，他們使用我們專利的 LNP 技術在其 COVID-19 mRNA-LNP 疫苗中。

本公司針對乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）的策略為開發一種功能性治癒方案，以imdusiran作為組合療法的潛在基石。截至目前為止的開發重點在於結合多種化合物，以抑制乙型肝炎病毒脫氧核糖核酸（HBV DNA）複製、乙型肝炎病毒核糖核酸（HBV RNA）轉錄以及乙型肝炎表面抗原（HBsAg）及其他病毒蛋白質的表現，同時增強患者的HBV特異性免疫反應，這些因素共同作用，可能解決實現功能性治癒的關鍵要素。功能性治癒被定義為在停藥後24週內，持續達到HBsAg血清清除且HBV DNA低於定量下限（<LLOQ），無論是否伴隨抗乙型肝炎表面抗體（anti-HBs）。對患有慢性乙型肝炎（cHBV）的患者而言，功能性治癒可預防HBV疾病進展的併發症，減少HBV負擔，透過降低患者污名化來改善現有有限且更有效的HBV治療方案，進一步提升長期預後並降低相關醫療成本。本公司目前持續評估HBV策略，也包含分析imdusiran潛在抑制HBV DNA複製及HBV RNA和HBsAg表現的能力，而無需任何免疫療法。我們也持續評估並優化imdusiran的潛在第二期b臨牀試驗設計。
本公司HBV產品開發路線圖包含以下項目：

•imdusiran（AB-729）為本公司專屬的GalNAc連結、皮下給藥的RNAi治療性產品候選藥物，可抑制所有HBV抗原，包括HBsAg，這被認為是啟動患者免疫系統對HBV反應的關鍵前提。在第一期及第二期a臨牀試驗中，已有超過200名患有cHBV感染的患者接受imdusiran治療。截至目前為止產生的臨牀數據顯示，imdusiran可顯著降低HBsAg及其他病毒蛋白質、HBV DNA及HBV RNA，並在部分患者中實現功能性治癒，同時具有良好的安全性與耐受性。在所有評估的HBV基因型（A至E）中，患者均觀察到效益。在第一期及第二期a臨牀試驗中，有八名患者在不接受任何治療的情況下，實現功能性治癒，其中包括兩名未接受任何pegylated interferon alfa-2a（IFN）作為組合療法的患者。在本公司第二期a臨牀試驗中，共有41名患者在停止NA治療後，至少持續48週不接受NA治療。在所有第二期a臨牀試驗的105名患者中，總共有47%（49/105）的患者實現功能性治癒或持續不接受NA治療。目前有18名患者正在進行長期追蹤（包括上述八名功能性治癒患者及10名停止治療並持續不接受NA治療的患者），其中一名停止NA治療的患者在長期追蹤期間實現功能性治癒，且89%的18名患者持續不接受NA治療達82至134週。兩名原始的八名功能性治癒患者在長期追蹤期間出現血清轉變，但仍保持病毒受抑制且不接受NA治療。此外，在另外11名有數據的患者中，他們在第二期a臨牀試驗中停止NA治療，但隨後提前終止長期追蹤，其中一名患者實現功能性治癒，兩名患者重新開始NA治療。截至目前為止，總共有10名患者在第二期a臨牀試驗及長期追蹤期間實現功能性治癒。

•AB-101為本公司專屬的口服PD-L1抑制劑，具有潛力透過抑制PD-L1來激活患者的HBV特異性免疫反應。AB-101目前處於第一期a/b臨牀試驗（AB-101-001），評估單劑及多劑口服給藥在健康受試者及患有cHBV感染患者的安全部分、耐受性、藥動學（PK）及藥效學（PD）。此臨牀試驗中健康受試者在第一及第二部分以及cHBV患者在第三部分的數據顯示，AB-101通常具有良好耐受性，並顯示出高受體佔有率的證據。

為協助將imdusiran定位為組合療法的潛在基石，本公司已完全招募兩項第二期a臨牀試驗，將imdusiran與其他藥物組合使用。這些試驗的目的是先以imdusiran降低HBsAg水平，再給予補充藥物，如免疫調節劑或治療性疫苗，進一步降低HBsAg水平並促進抗HBV免疫。我們認為，若能降低HBsAg及其他病毒抗原並促進免疫反應，我們可能實現持續HBsAg血清清除及HBV DNA <LLOQ，潛在地在患有cHBV的患者中實現功能性治癒。目前，患有cHBV的患者治療選擇有限，僅有NA治療，需終身治療，或有限時間的IFN治療，而IFN耐受性差且有嚴重的併發症與副作用。我們認為，即使未實現功能性治癒，患者若健康狀況允許，能停止NA治療並維持病毒受抑制，也能從imdusiran中獲得顯著效益。

在第二期a臨牀試驗中，有八名患有cHBV的患者在接受imdusiran與NA治療組合，並搭配IFN或低劑量nivolumab加免疫療法後實現功能性治癒。在這些八名患者中，有七名接受60mg劑量imdusiran治療的患者在基線時HBsAg水平低於1000 IU/mL。根據文獻，HBsAg水平低於1000 IU/mL的患者佔cHBV人口的顯著比例。截至目前為止，這八名患者中有六名持續維持功能性治癒，時間範圍為82至134週，而兩名患者出現血清轉變但仍保持病毒受抑制且不接受NA治療。除了在第二期a臨牀試驗中實現功能性治癒的患者外，還有41名患者在停止NA治療後，至少持續48週不接受NA治療。總計，在接受imdusiran治療後，所有第二期a臨牀試驗的105名患者中，有47%（49/105）的患者實現功能性治癒或持續不接受NA治療。目前在本公司延續研究中，有10名患者已停止NA治療並持續不接受NA治療至少48週，正在進行長期追蹤，其中一名患者在長期追蹤期間實現功能性治癒，總共有八名患者持續不接受NA治療達96至131週。這些結果顯示，imdusiran有助於患者維持病毒受抑制，並可能幫助患者在完成有限imdusiran治療方案後多年實現有益的臨牀結果。

本公司乙型肝炎（HBV）策略為開發一種功能性癒愈方法，用以治療慢性乙型肝炎（cHBV）感染患者，imdusiran 作為組合療法中潛在的基石。截至目前為止的開發重點為結合多種化合物，以抑制乙型肝炎病毒脫氧核糖核酸（HBV DNA）複製、乙型肝炎病毒核糖核酸（HBV RNA）轉錄、乙型肝炎表面抗原（HBsAg）及其他病毒蛋白質的表現，並增強患者對 HBV 的特定免疫反應，這些因素共同作用，可能解決達成功能性癒愈最重要的要素。功能性癒愈被定義為治療後 24 週持續 HBsAg 血清清除，且 HBV DNA 低於檢測下限（<LLOQ），不管是否具有抗乙型肝炎表面抗體（anti-HBs）。對 cHBV 患者而言，功能性癒愈可預防 HBV 疾病進展的併發症，減少 HBV 疾病負擔，透過降低患者社會污名，並解決對有限且更有效 HBV 治療的迫切需求，進一步改善長期預後並降低相關醫療成本。本公司目前持續評估 HBV 策略，也包含分析 imdusiran 抑制 HBV DNA 複製及 HBV RNA 和 HBsAg 表現的潛力，而無需任何免疫療法。我們也持續評估並優化 imdusiran 的潛在第二期b臨牀試驗設計。
本公司產品管線包含以下計畫：

超過 200 名 cHBV 感染患者已於第一期及第二期a臨牀試驗中接受 imdusiran 治療。截至目前為止產生的臨牀數據顯示，imdusiran 可顯著降低 HBsAg 及其他病毒蛋白質、HBV DNA 及 HBV RNA，並在部分患者中達成功能性癒愈，同時為一般安全且耐受良好。在所有評估的 HBV 基因型（A 到 E）中，患者均觀察到效益。在第一期及第二期a臨牀試驗中，有八名患者在未接受任何治療的情況下達成功能性癒愈，這些患者接受包含 imdusiran 的組合療法，其中兩名患者未接受任何 pegylated 幹擾素 alfa-2a（IFN）作為組合療法的一部分。在第二期a臨牀試驗中，有 41 名患者在停止核苷（酸）類逆轉錄酶抑制劑（NA）治療後，至少持續 48 週不接受 NA 治療。在第二期a臨牀試驗中，總共有 47%（49/105）的患者達成功能性癒愈或持續不接受 NA 治療。目前有 18 名患者正在進行長期追蹤（包括上述的八名功能性癒愈患者及 10 名停止治療並持續不接受 NA 治療的患者），其中一名停止 NA 治療的患者在長期追蹤期間達成功能性癒愈，且 89% 的 18 名患者持續不接受 NA 治療，時間為 82 到 134 週。兩名原始的八名功能性癒愈患者在長期追蹤期間出現血清轉變，但仍然維持病毒受抑制且不接受 NA 治療。此外，在另外 11 名有資料的患者中，他們在第二期a臨牀試驗中停止 NA 治療，但隨後提前停止長期追蹤，其中一名患者達成功能性癒愈，兩名患者重新開始 NA 治療。截至目前為止，在第二期a臨牀試驗及長期追蹤期間，總共有 10 名患者達成功能性癒愈。

AB-101 是本公司專屬的口服 PD-L1 抑制劑，具有潛力透過抑制 PD-L1 來活化患者的 HBV 特定免疫反應。AB-101 目前正在進行第一期a/第一期b 臨牀試驗（AB-101-001），評估單劑及多劑口服給藥在健康受試者及 cHBV 感染患者的安安全性、耐受性、藥動學（PK）及藥效學（PD）。此臨牀試驗中健康受試者在第一及第二部分及 cHBV 患者在第三部分的數據顯示，AB-101 通常耐受良好，並顯示出高受體佔有率的證據。
與齊魯藥業股份有限公司（Qilu）的合作
2021 年 12 月，本公司與 Qilu 簽訂技術轉移及授權協議（Qilu 授權協議），根據此協議，本公司授予 Qilu 一個可轉讓、需支付版稅的授權，根據本公司所有的智慧財產權，此授權在開發及製造方面為非獨佔，而在商業化 imdusiran，包括包含 imdusiran 的藥物產品，用於中國、香港、澳門及臺灣（大中華及臺灣）地區治療或預防乙型肝炎。

headings: 與本公司業務、財務結果及需要額外資金有關之風險
我們面臨與Moderna和解協議下附條件結算付款有關之風險。
我們仍處於發展初期階段，目前可供您評估產品候選藥物之資訊有限。
自我們成立以來，幾乎每個年度我們均產生營運虧損，且我們預期在可預見之未來內將無法實現營運獲利。截至目前為止，我們尚未有產品收入。
我們尚未從產品銷售中產生收入，且可能永遠無法從營運中實現獲利。
與產品候選藥物之開發、臨牀試驗、監管核准、行銷及保險給付與 reimbursment 有關之風險
由於我們之運營資源有限，我們可能選擇追求某個產品候選藥物，而未能推進後續顯示更高臨牀與商業成功機會之產品候選藥物。
我們若干臨牀試驗目前或曾於美國境外進行，且美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）可能不接受於美國境外進行之試驗資料。
本公司無法保證監管機構審查我們產品候選藥物申請所需時間，且我們可能無法取得必要的監管許可以行銷產品候選藥物。
若某產品候選藥物導致不希望的副作用，則我們可能無法取得該產品候選藥物的監管許可或進行商業化。
我們可能難以招募患者參與臨牀試驗，這可能會延誤或阻礙我們產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗。
即使我們的產品候選藥物取得監管許可，它們仍將受到持續的監管要求與監督。
我們面臨來自其他針對乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）的生物科技與製藥公司的重大競爭。
本公司產生產品收入並實現營運獲利的能力， largely dependent on 未來產品候選藥物的商業成功。
我們可能產生重大賠償責任，並可能被要求限制產品的商業化以應對產品賠償訴訟。
對於我們的產品候選藥物可能無法提供保險覆蓋與足夠的報銷，這可能會使我們難以以獲利方式銷售產品。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險與不確定性。上述任何風險與不確定性，無論單獨發生或共同發生，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果或前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市價可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。上述所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。一般性適用的風險與不確定性，以及目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果或前景造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司參與專利侵權訴訟，以保護並主張我們的智慧財產權權利，對抗大型且資金充足的公司與美國政府，這需要本公司持續投入大量資源，且本公司可能無法在這些程序中取得成功。

本公司目前正參與一項專利侵權訴訟，對象為美國的輝瑞/ BioNTech，若 Moderna 提起訴訟，則為 Moderna 的 §1498 上訴，這些為對抗大型且資金充足的公司的行動。本公司同時也參與一項訴訟，對象為美國政府，於美國聯邦法院聲請賠償，因 Moderna 的專利侵權行為，其疫苗劑量已售予美國政府，並根據地方法院的判決，被認為是直接提供給美國政府員工的劑量。這些訴訟中的一些已經持續多年，並需要大量資源投入。本公司預期這些程序將在一段漫長的時間內持續，並需要類似的資源投入。每項程序的結果都面臨高度不確定性，這取決於特定的事實與法律解釋。本公司認為持續追訴這些行動對我們未來的成功至關重要，並有意繼續進行。每項行動將導致法院對重大問題作出判決與決定，例如聲請解釋、專利有效性、侵權、§1498 的抗辯、管轄權及其他事項，幾乎所有這些問題都可能受到上訴程序的影響，而這些程序通常耗時且結果難以預測。此外，一項程序的判決或決定並不一定代表另一項程序的判決或決定，即使事實與法律問題相似。本公司預期各法院將在未來一年內發布重大判決，這些判決的揭露可能導致本公司股票價格出現顯著波動，並可能影響本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果。

除了應支付給本公司與 Genevant 的總計 950.0 百萬美元非條件性賠償金外，Moderna 賠償協議還規定，本公司與 Genevant 可能獲得最高總計 1.3 十億美元的條件性賠償金，此金額僅在 Arbutus/Genevant §1498 賠償勝訴（如上所定義）的情況下支付。若上訴法院判決 §1498 阻止本公司與 Genevant 的全部或部分聲請，本公司可能完全無法獲得付款，或僅能獲得 1.3 十億美元條件性賠償金的按比例支付。雖然 Moderna 根據現代化賠償協議負有財務約束，以確保條件性賠償金的支付，但本公司與 Genevant 並無保證能及時或完全獲得此筆付款，或因超出本公司控制範圍的因素，包括合同條件的履行、行政或程序上的延誤，或對協議解釋或執行的爭議。此外，根據現代化賠償協議中規定的某些情況，若 Arbutus/Genevant §1498 賠償勝訴後，最終且不可上訴的判決判斷 Moderna 勝訴，本公司與 Genevant 將被要求歸還已收到的條件性賠償金，並支付利息。任何歸還義務可能導致本公司使用大量現金。此外，本公司所收到的條件性賠償金可能受到財務約束，以保護條件性賠償金的潛在歸還，這將限制本公司在該期間內自由使用這些資金。現代化 §1498 上訴及任何相關後續上訴，其結果面臨高度不確定性，包括其時間安排，本公司無法保證能實現 Arbutus/Genevant §1498 賠償勝訴。如需更多資訊，請參閱「項目 1 – 經營業務 – 其他合作夥伴、版稅權利與智慧財產權訴訟」及「項目 3 – 法律程序」。
